title: Discrete time crystals in disordered anisotropic Heisenberg chains
authors: Francesco Formicola, Grazia Di Bello, Antonio De Candia, Giulio De Filippis, Carmine Antonio Perroni
abstract: A discrete time crystal is an out-of-equilibrium phase of matter characterized by the spontaneous breaking of discrete time-translation symmetry. Using extensive numerical simulations based on matrix-product-state methods, we provide evidence for discrete time-crystalline behavior in strongly disordered spin chains with Heisenberg interactions, including the isotropic point, subject to periodic driving. Starting from a many-body localized regime, we observe that rotations induced by delta kicks produce a pronounced subharmonic response at half the drive frequency in spin observables. We investigate the stability of this response against rotation-angle errors through entanglement entropy, quantum Fisher information, short-range spin correlations, and restricted-control ergotropy. Increasing the rotation error reveals an intermediate dynamical regime separating the time-crystalline and Floquet-localized responses. In this regime, most observables exhibit signatures of weakly correlated dynamics reminiscent of Anderson localization.
summary: This research explores discrete time-crystalline phases in disordered Heisenberg spin chains driven periodically. Using advanced MPS simulations, the authors confirm the DTC signature but show that increasing the driving error suppresses this phase. The study maps out an intermediate dynamical regime characterized by localization signatures, providing a detailed diagnostic toolkit for non-equilibrium quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and stability of discrete time-crystalline (DTC) behavior in strongly disordered anisotropic Heisenberg spin chains subjected to periodic driving.
main_result: DTC behavior is observed at zero driving error, characterized by period-doubled oscillations, but this response is suppressed by increasing the rotation error, leading to a regime reminiscent of Anderson localization.
method: The study employs extensive numerical simulations using Matrix Product States (MPS) and Matrix Product Operators (MPO) to analyze time evolution.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional disordered spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain driven by global $\pi$-kicks. The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor interactions and random on-site fields.
key_observables: Two-time imbalance correlation function ($G_2(0, t)$), Entanglement entropy, Quantum Fisher information, and Restricted-control ergotropy.
important_parameters: The rotation-angle error ($\epsilon$), disorder strength ($W$), and the ratio of interaction couplings ($J_z/J_{\perp}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be accurately described using MPS techniques and the two-site time-dependent variational principle (2TDVP).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the imbalance correlation function $G_2(0, t)$ and its dependence on the driving cycle $n$, comparing DTC signatures against localization signatures across varying error parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the theoretical framework of spontaneous symmetry breaking in Floquet systems to numerical simulations on the disordered spin chain, analyzing the robustness of the DTC phase against controlled errors and comparing diagnostics across different physical regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium quantum phases (time crystals) in the presence of disorder, bridging concepts from many-body localization, Floquet engineering, and quantum criticality, which are highly relevant to modern AMO and condensed matter research.
